literature_only_consent: Use fictional, published, de-identified, openly licensed, or otherwise authorised teaching material. Obtain any consent and institutional clearance required for real-world material outside this app. This workshop does not create, replace, or interpret a clinical consent form.

Doctors.headline: Spend workshop time on clinical judgement, not prompt engineering.
Doctors.copy: Practise copy-ready prompts, specialty cases, source checking, and AI-versus-doctor review using fictional data.
Doctors.cta: Join the hands-on AI Rx session for doctors.
Doctors.platform_post: AI can draft and organise. The doctor still decides. AI Rx gives physicians copy-ready prompts, specialty-specific fictional cases, and structured AI-versus-doctor debriefs anchored in patient safety.

Hospital leaders.headline: Move from scattered experimentation to governed clinical decision support.
Hospital leaders.copy: Use the workshop to examine privacy, accountability, evidence, workflow ownership, exceptions, and measurable patient-service impact.
Hospital leaders.cta: Bring a clinical, IT, quality, and governance team.
Hospital leaders.platform_post: AI adoption in hospitals needs more than a tool demonstration. AI Rx connects use cases with data boundaries, qualified review, human override, audit trails, and patient-centred measures.

Researchers.headline: Use AI to accelerate evidence work without outsourcing critical appraisal.
Researchers.copy: Build PICO questions, literature searches, evidence tables, and journal-club discussions while checking every citation and inference.
Researchers.cta: Bring one authorised paper set and one research question.
Researchers.platform_post: Source-grounded is not the same as scientifically correct. AI Rx trains researchers to use AI for discovery and synthesis while retaining transparent methods, source verification, and uncertainty.

Medical educators.headline: Teach where AI stops and professional reasoning begins.
Medical educators.copy: Use staged cases, copy-ready prompts, AI-versus-doctor comparisons, polls, and reflection to make tacit clinical reasoning discussable.
Medical educators.cta: Adapt the specialty cases for your learner level.
Medical educators.platform_post: The useful teaching moment is not a perfect AI answer. It is the gap between the AI draft and the clinician's judgement. AI Rx turns that gap into a structured debrief.

Pharma and life sciences.headline: Communicate evidence clearly while preserving medical, regulatory, and audience boundaries.
Pharma and life sciences.copy: Practise literature synthesis, audience-specific education, content review, and disclosure without turning workshop material into promotional clinical advice.
Pharma and life sciences.cta: Use the research and communication labs with approved sources.
Pharma and life sciences.platform_post: AI Rx helps medical and life-sciences teams convert authorised evidence into reviewable educational drafts, with source checks, audience fit, disclosure, and human approval built into the workflow.

ethics_topics.title: Patient confidentiality
ethics_topics.description: Use data minimisation, approved environments, role-based access, and explicit policy. De-identification reduces but may not remove risk.

ethics_topics.title: Consent
ethics_topics.description: Explain what the tool does, what data it receives, choices available, and what happens after processing.

ethics_topics.title: Hallucination
ethics_topics.description: Compare material outputs with the source and treat unsupported details as safety failures, not stylistic errors.

ethics_topics.title: Automation bias
ethics_topics.description: Design review steps that make disagreement, uncertainty, and escalation visible before action.

ethics_topics.title: Population bias
ethics_topics.description: Check evidence in the intended population, prevalence, equipment, language, setting, and workflow.

ethics_topics.title: Explainability
ethics_topics.description: Users need enough information to understand intended output, limits, and appropriate response. A heatmap alone is not an explanation.

ethics_topics.title: Source verification
ethics_topics.description: Open cited material and check that each claim matches the source, population, date, and evidence type.

ethics_topics.title: Copyright
ethics_topics.description: Use authorised or openly licensed documents, images, and media. Format conversion does not change rights.

ethics_topics.title: Institutional policy
ethics_topics.description: Local approval, procurement, information security, legal review, clinical governance, and audit requirements still apply.

ethics_topics.title: Medical-device regulation
ethics_topics.description: Verify the exact product, version, intended use, indication, geography, and current listing. Do not generalise from company-level claims.

ethics_topics.title: Clinical accountability
ethics_topics.description: A qualified professional owns review and final use. AI generation does not transfer responsibility.

ethics_topics.title: Audit trails and override
ethics_topics.description: Record material inputs, versions, reviews, changes, exceptions, and who authorised the final action.

session_feedback.privacy_note: Please do not include patient-identifiable, confidential, or institutionally restricted information in your response.
